title: Leading Team Members Who Are Truth Tellers
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece offers guidance for managing team members who prioritize blunt candor over tact, often bright and substantive contributors whose unfiltered delivery causes collateral damage in meetings. The recommended approach is showing them the cause-and-effect of their unedited comments and asking a reframing question about how to express candid views so others actually want to hear more of them. Because full behavioral transformation is unlikely, the piece also recommends giving truth-tellers a dedicated venue to express unfiltered views privately. It closes by framing this as a teaching relationship where directness is reframed as most valuable when paired with consideration for context.
points: Truth-telling team members often add real substance but damage relationships through unfiltered delivery.
The first step is showing them the cause-and-effect impact of their unedited comments.
A key reframing question asks how to express candor so others want to hear more of it.
Because full transformation is unlikely, leaders are advised to give truth-tellers a dedicated private venue for unfiltered views.
quotes: Managing a team member who contributes unedited and unfiltered viewpoints often means doing damage repair after meetings and conversations.
Most truth-tellers lack empathy, self-awareness, and perspective.
The first move is to show them the cause and effect of their choice not to edit.
How can I best express my candid view so others will want to hear more of it?
By showing them the benefit of restraint, truth-tellers slowly lose their faith in the false binary between unedited truth and integrity.
As with many team member challenges, the difference in learning is usually effective leadership.
